13:The main window's body: the area to the right of the project sidebar, where the tasks sent to the harness, and the files opened in tabs beside them, are shown, and the chat input they are sent from.
18:The [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) lives within the body, along its bottom: its left edge against the project sidebar, and above it, beneath the body's tab bar, the selected tab's contents: the message list, or an open file. While a task runs, the [RightSidebarScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) runs the body's full height at its right, beside the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there, the chat input reaches the window's right edge.
23:Whenever something slides out or back along one of the body's edges, as the [RightSidebarScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) does, everything else in the body moves smoothly with it, frame by frame, rather than jumping once the slide is over: the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, the Ask conversation while it shows, and the chat input all keep their right edge against the sliding edge throughout, so they narrow or widen together, in step with it and with each other. None of them lags behind another, is left at its old width until the slide settles, or runs beneath what is sliding. Their contents are laid out anew at each width as it changes, text wrapping and rows reflowing as they go: the tab bar's tabs, the chat input's text and buttons, the message list's table, and an open file's editor. A slide that reverses partway moves them back from wher

33:- a task view for each task opened in a tab of its own, as its task tabs say, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
34:- the [AskConversationScope](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope), in the Chat tab's place beneath the tab bar, while the chat input's Ask tab is selected
35:- the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), along the bottom beneath whichever tab is selected, and beneath the Ask conversation too
36:- the [RightSidebarScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope), at the right of all of these, the tab bar and the chat input included, while a task runs or is queued, or it is opened by hand
40:## Ask Mode
42:While the chat input's Ask tab is selected, the Ask conversation, as the [AskConversationScope](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) says, takes the Chat tab's place in the body, filling all of it beneath the tab bar and above the chat input, as the message list fills it for every other mode: the body never splits, and nothing is shown beside the conversation. The Chat tab then reads "Ask" in Ask's colour. Selecting another mode's tab brings the message list back in its place, as it was left, and selecting Ask again brings the conversation back, scrolled where it was; the switch is at once, with nothing sliding. A file or task tab selected shows that file or task whatever mode is selected, and selecting Ask while one is shown selects the Chat tab, so the conversation is in view.
46:Along the top of the body runs a tab bar, in gpui-kit's default tab styling, across the width the message list takes: from the project sidebar to the right sidebar while a task runs, and to the window's right edge otherwise. Its first tab, Chat, shows the message list, and is always there: it can't be closed or moved. After it comes a tab for each open file and each task opened in a tab of its own, files and tasks together, in the order they were opened unless they have been dragged since, scrolling sideways once there are more than fit.
52:## Task Tabs
54:The Chat tab shows only the task the harness is working on now, and those running beside it, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s header shows them, or, while none runs, the task that finished last, until the next is sent. It never shows any other task: a task opened from the right sidebar's Tasks tab, as the [TasksTabScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.md#tasks-tab-scope) says, or from anywhere else that opens a task, opens in a tab of its own in the body's tab bar, as a file does: a task not open yet gets a new tab just after the one selected, and is selected; opening one that already has a tab selects that tab; and opening the task Chat is showing selects Chat instead.
55:A task's tab is laid out as a file's is: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left in its mode's colour, its status, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, then its name, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis at 24 characters, then its close button. Hovering it shows its prompt's first lines and its mode as its tooltip. It can be dragged among the files' tabs, and closed as they are, closing it changing nothing about the task.
56:Beneath it, the task shows as it would at the head of the Chat tab, on its own: its header, with its status, time, compiled prompt, and buttons, then its output table, then the files it changed, scrolled to its top the first time it is shown, and as it was left after. A task still running shows its output as it comes, its table locked to the bottom while scrolled there, as the latest task's is, and carries on in its tab whether or not the tab is selected. Its tab stays open once it finishes. Opening a task in a tab doesn't select it in the Chat tab or change what Chat shows, and Chat's running tasks are never opened in tabs of their own unless asked for, a running task opened from the Tasks tab selecting it in Chat's header instead. Each open project keeps its own task tabs, as its file tabs are kept, and none is reopened when the project is opened again.
62:Closing a file's tab, with its close button or the editor's, closes the file, the editor first asking to discard any unsaved changes. Closing the selected tab selects the tab to its right, or, with none to its right, the one to its left, which is Chat once no file is left. Closing a tab that isn't selected leaves the selection as it is.

commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Ask mode no longer splits the body. With Ask selected, the Ask conversation takes the Chat tab's place, filling everything between the tab bar and the chat input. The build is clean and the rewritten Ask test passes. In the full run the only failure besides that test was the quit-while-running test, which passed on its own.

- **Switching modes:** another mode brings the message list back as you left it, and Ask brings the conversation back, with nothing sliding. Each is rendered fresh in place, so the conversation's scroll position is kept only as far as its list already keeps it; I didn't test that it survives the switch.
- **File and task tabs:** they still show their file or task in any mode. Picking Ask while one is selected switches to the Chat tab so the conversation is in view.
- **Reading width:** questions and answers sit in a centred column at most 760px wide.

The changes are in `src/prompt_mode.rs` and `src/prompt_mode/ask_pane.rs`. I rewrote the old split test to check the conversation fills the message list's place. One other test now counts the task's rows before switching to Ask, since the task's output no longer shows beside the conversation. This follows the spec, which matches your prompt.
